title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
BAMOR explores the potential of applying bamboo and other naturally elastic materials to responsive soft robotic architecture. Unlike conventional temporary performance installations that primarily rely on industrial materials and static structures, the project utilizes the inherent flexibility of bamboo to construct a lightweight, deployable bamboo–textile structure that is easy to transport and assemble, and applies it to a small-scale performance and viewing space.

The system enhances the relationship between people and space through two modes of interaction: in everyday use, the installation recognizes users’ postures and positions in real time and adaptively adjusts its spatial form to accommodate different needs for rest and activity; in performance settings, the installation captures the tempo and beats of music in real time, driving the structural blades to produce rhythmic dynamic responses, allowing the space itself to participate in the performance and enhancing the immersive experience of performers and audiences.

BAMOR thus combines natural materials, lightweight deployable structures, and real-time interaction, while reducing the environmental impact of temporary installations through the renewable and biodegradable material life cycle of bamboo, exploring a more sustainable dynamic architectural environment with sensing and responsive capabilities.

BAMOR 探索将竹材等天然弹性材料用于响应式软体机器人建筑的可能性。项目利用竹材自身的柔韧性，构建轻质、可展开、便于运输与组装的竹—织物结构，将其应用于小型表演与观看空间。

系统通过两种交互模式加强人与空间的联系：日常使用时，装置实时识别使用者的姿态与位置，并调整空间形态，以适应休息和活动需求；表演时，装置实时捕捉音乐节奏与节拍，驱动结构叶片产生律动，让空间参与表演，增强表演者和观众的沉浸体验。

BAMOR 将天然材料、轻质可展开结构和实时交互结合，并通过竹材可再生、可生物降解的材料生命周期，探索降低临时装置环境影响的可能性，构建具有感知与响应能力的动态建筑环境。

Siyi Mao , Yuhe Shi , Zhengzhen Zhang, Jiahong Zheng

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
This project explores sensor-driven motor control using Arduino and ROS2. An ultrasonic distance sensor provides real-time input, which is used to control a Dynamixel motor and actuate a kinetic structure. A threshold-based control strategy with a buffer zone (hysteresis-like logic) is implemented to improve stability and avoid rapid switching.
Key variables include distance (cm), threshold_close = 25 cm, threshold_open = 35 cm, threshold_stop = 60 cm, current_state (close / open / stop), and motor velocity commands. When the distance is less than 25 cm, the structure closes (Motor Velocity=+80); when between 35 cm and 60 cm, it opens(Motor Velocity=-80); and when above 60 cm, the motor stops(Motor Velocity=0). The buffer zone between 25 cm and 35 cm ensures smoother transitions.

本项目探索基于 Arduino 与 ROS2 的传感器驱动电机控制。超声波距离传感器提供实时输入，控制 Dynamixel 电机并驱动动态结构。系统采用带缓冲区的阈值控制策略，以提高稳定性、避免快速切换。

关键参数包括距离、25 cm 的闭合阈值、35 cm 的打开阈值、60 cm 的停止阈值、当前状态及电机速度。当距离小于 25 cm 时，结构闭合（速度 +80）；距离为 35–60 cm 时打开（速度 −80）；距离超过 60 cm 时停止。25–35 cm 的缓冲区使状态过渡更加平稳。

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
In a world where architecture breathes and infrastructure grows, Urban Mycelium envisions a city interwoven with living light. Each organism—part fungus, part technology—forms a network of bioluminescent structures that clean the air, guide the night, and nurture public life.

From the floating Aerolume that purifies the atmosphere, to the grounding Glowstool that invites rest, these luminous hybrids reimagine urban ecology as a living, evolving organism.

Urban Mycelium 构想一座建筑能够呼吸、基础设施能够生长的城市：介于真菌与技术之间的生物发光结构形成网络，净化空气、引导夜间活动，并滋养公共生活。

从漂浮并净化大气的 Aerolume，到扎根地面、邀请人们休息的 Glowstool，这些发光的混合体将城市生态重新想象为不断演化的生命体。

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
Memory Museum explores how human memory has evolved alongside cultural and technological development. Beginning with Matteo Ricci’s Memory Palace and Bernard Stiegler’s theory of primary, secondary, and tertiary memory, the project translates different modes of remembering into architectural experiences.

Three interconnected programmes—a government meeting space, a religious space, and an archaeological research institute—correspond respectively to immediate memory, long-term personal memory, and technologically externalised memory. Through overlapping programmes, shifting thresholds, material transitions, light, and different forms of exhibition, these abstract processes of memory are transformed into a continuous spatial narrative.

Rather than treating memory as something contained solely within the mind, the museum traces its transformation from immediate perception and personal recollection to externalised technological storage. Designed as an expandable structure extending towards the Meiguan Ancient Road, the architecture itself grows and accumulates over time, echoing the evolving nature of human memory.
Memory Museum 探索人类记忆如何随文化与技术发展而演变。项目从利玛窦的记忆宫殿与贝尔纳·斯蒂格勒关于第一、第二和第三记忆的理论出发，将不同的记忆方式转化为建筑体验。政府议事空间、宗教空间和考古研究机构相互连接，分别对应即时记忆、个人长期记忆和技术外化记忆。通过功能叠合、阈限变化、材料、光线与展陈方式，建筑形成连续的空间叙事，并以朝梅关古道延伸的可扩展结构回应记忆不断积累与演变的过程。

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
Interest in the use of kinetic envelopes in architecture has grown in recent years. On the one hand, digital design processes are available to bring kinetic concepts to life. On the other hand, there is a desire to have active building elements to regulate building performance and create a more comfortable built environment. The advent of digital design processes has made the concept of kinetic energy a reality.

This design explores the design and application of an adaptive facade in a specific context, the Suzhou region, which is located in a subtropical monsoon climate. Specifically, the design results are presented in terms of geometry, kinetic systems, energy conversion and adaptive shading effects. 

When analysing the different energy flows, solar radiation is of particular interest. The mediation of solar radiation has the potential to reduce heating and cooling requirements while distributing daylight according to the wishes of the occupants. In addition, the use of thin-film photovoltaic panels as kinetic energy elements enables facades to act as generators. In some cases, this technology can offset the energy consumption of the spaces behind the envelope, increasing the sustainability of the building while creating a more comfortable indoor environment.
本项目以亚热带季风气候下的苏州为背景，探索自适应建筑立面的设计与应用，涵盖几何构成、运动系统、能量转换与动态遮阳。通过调节太阳辐射，立面在降低采暖和制冷需求的同时，为使用者提供适宜的自然采光。薄膜光伏板作为可运动构件，使建筑表皮兼具发电能力，以提升建筑可持续性与室内舒适度。

projects.name: Moon Metabolism

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
As humanity continues to advance in space exploration, the Moon has become a key target for establishing long-term human settlements. The vision of creating a sustainable human presence on the Moon has gained global attention, driven by organizations like NASA and the European Space Agency. With significant progress in space technology, constructing a permanent lunar base is now a tangible goal. This presents new challenges in ensuring human survival, including addressing the extreme environmental conditions and creating self-sustaining habitats.

The Moon's environment differs greatly from Earth's, with extreme temperature fluctuations, radiation exposure, and no atmospheric protection. However, areas such as the Moon's south pole, particularly the permanently sunlit regions, present ideal locations for establishing a lunar settlement. Additionally, lava tubes found on the Moon provide natural shelter, offering protection from radiation and temperature extremes, making them a promising foundation for constructing a habitat.

This project proposes a sustainable lunar settlement, the "Moon Village," designed to support long-term human habitation. The settlement will be built within the Moon's lava tubes, taking advantage of their natural insulation. Modular and inflatable structures will be used to create flexible living spaces, minimizing transportation and construction costs. Solar energy and self-sustaining greenhouse systems will provide the necessary resources for energy and food.

The design also incorporates robotic construction and 3D printing technologies, which will be used for expanding the settlement as human presence on the Moon grows. This proposal offers a feasible approach to lunar habitation, focusing on sustainability, flexibility, and long-term expansion.

本项目探索支持长期居住的可持续月球聚落。月球极端温差、辐射与缺乏大气保护的环境，对居住系统提出挑战；南极区域的日照条件和熔岩管的天然防护能力，为聚落选址提供了可能。

方案将主要居住空间置于熔岩管内，利用天然隔热与防辐射条件。模块化和可充气结构提供灵活的居住空间，并降低运输与建造成本。太阳能与温室系统支持能源和食物供给。

机器人建造和 3D 打印支持聚落随人口增长而扩展，形成强调可持续性、灵活性与长期发展的月球居住设想。

projects.name: Generic & Traditional

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
A neighborhood center provides multifunctional services for the community, promoting interaction and meeting daily needs. This concept is widely applied in Singapore and Suzhou Industrial Park, enhancing accessibility and social connections through compact design. As global urbanization accelerates, cities are becoming more standardized, often at the cost of local culture and history. The Shantang area in Suzhou, a key cultural landmark, serves both as a residential space and a tourist destination, fostering a diverse community of locals and visitors.

Generic & Traditional explores the tension between modern urban development and cultural identity preservation through three core principles: efficiency, inclusivity, and regionalism. Inspired by Rem Koolhaas's “Generic City” concept, which prioritizes efficiency and globalization, neighborhood centers are functional hubs but often lack a unique identity. In Suzhou, the challenge is integrating modern practicality with the cultural and historical significance of places like Shantang Street and the ancient city walls.
Through three core principles—efficiency, inclusivity, and regionalism—Generic & Traditional explores this tension and bridges the divide between Suzhou’s past and present, creating a space that is both functional and meaningful.

The design integrates modern needs with local heritage by combining flexible, modular spaces with historical and cultural elements of the site. The use of local materials, like recycled bricks and wood, and the layout that responds to the natural and historical context of the area, reflects a commitment to regionalism and sustainability. This approach fosters a dynamic environment where modernity and tradition coexist, providing a space that serves the community’s diverse needs while respecting its heritage.

邻里中心通过多功能服务促进社区交往、满足日常需求。全球城市化提升了效率，也可能削弱地方文化与历史。苏州山塘地区兼具居住与旅游功能，为探索现代城市发展与文化身份之间的张力提供了背景。

Generic & Traditional 围绕效率、包容性和地域性展开，借鉴雷姆·库哈斯“通用城市”的讨论，思考如何把现代功能需求与山塘街、古城墙的历史意义结合。

设计以灵活模块空间回应日常使用，并通过回收砖、木材及顺应场地历史环境的布局，将地方材料和文化记忆融入当代邻里中心，让现代性与传统并存。

subtitle: Neighborhood Center Design: Exploring the tension between modern urban development and the preservation of cultural identity
邻里中心设计：现代城市发展与文化身份保护之间的张力

projects.name: Parametric Robotic Construction

title: Project brief
项目简介
text: This collaborative project combines modern robotic technology with parametric design, using Grasshopper-generated parametric curves to precisely construct a brick wall with a robotic arm. The design not only demonstrates the application of digital tools in architecture but also explores how to achieve precise construction and structural stability in complex curved forms. The efficiency and flexibility of the robotic arm offer unprecedented possibilities for architectural design, driving innovation in construction methods.
这个合作项目将机器人技术与参数化设计结合，利用 Grasshopper 生成参数化曲线，通过机械臂精确建造砖墙。项目探索数字工具在建筑中的应用，以及复杂曲面形态中的建造精度与结构稳定性，研究机械臂的效率和灵活性为建筑建造带来的可能。

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
This project aims to support rural revitalization in China by addressing challenges like economic stagnation, aging populations, and rural-urban migration. It explores how architecture can create sustainable infrastructure that strengthens local industries, fosters community connections, and attracts tourism.

Nanwang Village, near Taihu Lake in Suzhou, lies at the crossroads between the village core and surrounding farmland. Known for its scenic landscapes and fruit industry, the site features production chains, packaging facilities, and roadside markets. Temporary constructions showcase the villagers' ingenuity, while spatial activities, such as informal gatherings and fruit harvesting, highlight the dynamic interplay of rural life and built form. These phenomena inspired the concept of "interlace," symbolizing the interaction between people, nature, and architecture.

Public functions like markets and event spaces align with main routes, while guesthouses near farmland offer privacy and nature immersion. Diverse unit typologies accommodate various needs, incorporating terraces, green roofs, and flexible installations inspired by temporary structures. Sustainable strategies, including steel frames, passive cooling, and green infrastructure, enhance energy efficiency and reduce impact.

The project envisions a vibrant hub where visitors experience authentic rural life, villagers gain economic opportunities, and architecture fosters sustainable development and cultural integration.

本项目关注中国乡村振兴中的经济停滞、人口老龄化与城乡迁移问题，探索建筑如何通过可持续基础设施支持本地产业、社区交往与旅游发展。

基地位于苏州太湖附近的南旺村，连接村庄中心与周边农田。当地果业生产、包装设施、路边集市与村民自建的临时设施，共同呈现乡村生活与建成环境的联系，启发了人与自然、建筑相互交织的“interlace”概念。

集市与活动空间沿主要流线布局，靠近农田的客房提供私密性和自然体验。不同单元结合露台、绿化屋顶及灵活设施，适应多种需求；钢框架、被动降温和绿色基础设施提升环境表现。

项目希望成为连接乡村体验、经济机会与文化交流的公共节点。

projects.name: Underground Theater

title: Project brief
项目简介
text:
Plato's Cave is the first cinema of mankind; the design concept of this project begins with the allegory of Plato's Cave, where one sees both the consciously presented world and the shadow of the real world. Virtual light and shadow are projected in the dark, soundproof cinema space underground, while real sunlight slants down in the open, continuous public space, accompanied by cultural and social spaces。

The operation of modern cinema is closely tied to capital and consumption, often serving a single purpose. Research shows the venue is near a residential area in the Hongkou district of Shanghai, with a rich urban history, and is close to the first cinema in the area. Cinemas take up less space than theatres and are more accessible to the public, making them more suitable for this venue's size and location.

Based on this, the design proposes the idea of a 'beacon of culture', focusing on activities before and after the film to transform the cinema into a multifunctional space. This allows for a cultural experience beyond the usual single-function model. Activities like exhibitions, readings, and coffee can be added to the darkened space, before, during, or after the film, creating a more dynamic environment. The experience culminates in a transition from virtual to real light and shadow, encouraging exploration and understanding of the real world through communication, rather than just eating and shopping like in a mall.

项目以柏拉图的洞穴寓言为起点，探讨被呈现的世界与真实世界的影像。地下隔音影院投射虚拟光影，地上的开放公共空间则引入真实日光，并连接文化与社交活动。

基地位于上海虹口居住区附近，具有丰富的城市历史，靠近当地早期电影院。相较剧场，电影院对空间的需求更紧凑，也更贴近公众生活。

设计提出“文化灯塔”的概念，通过观影前后的活动，将单一影院转化为多功能公共场所。展览、阅读和咖啡等功能延展观影体验，从虚拟光影走向真实光影，鼓励人们通过交流探索现实世界。

subtitle:
Plato's Cave and the beacon of culture: 
The concept of anti-commercial residential cinema and public space

intro: Selected projects, writing and other work.
about:
Weiyi Wang has a background in architecture, with interests spanning architectural design, emerging architectural technologies, and architectural theory. She is particularly interested in how technology participates in the design of space, and how its integration into architecture may reshape the ways people experience and remember space.

She received her undergraduate education in Architecture at Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University and later pursued an MArch in Architectural Design at The Bartlett, UCL. Across design and research, she brings together spatial design, technological experimentation, and theoretical inquiry, exploring topics ranging from culture and memory and future habitats to computational design, responsive environments, and human–machine interaction.

王惟毅拥有建筑学背景。她的兴趣横跨建筑设计、新兴建筑技术与建筑理论，尤其关注技术如何参与空间设计，以及技术介入如何改变人们体验和记忆空间的方式。

她本科毕业于西交利物浦大学建筑学专业，随后于伦敦大学学院巴特莱特建筑学院攻读建筑设计硕士。在设计与研究中，她结合空间设计、技术实验与理论思考，探索从文化与记忆、未来人居到计算设计、响应式环境与人机交互等不同议题。

title: The Redistribution of Spatial Memory
空间记忆的重新分配
